notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (authored_by kind model, model_id deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run_id wC-031; reviewed_by null); no hardware or sim run was made. The card's entry symbol was confirmed: causal_world/envs/causalworld.py:18 defines class CausalWorld(gym.Env); the native surface used by the bridge is reset, step, seed and close, and the device is simulated R0 with no hardware stop path. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD (mock strategy only; decision family-config and helper GymnasiumDriver unchanged): the card's preferred upstream-sim backend was not usable. CausalWorld registers no gym.make id (the documented factory is CausalWorld(task=generate_task(...)), README.md:215), the clone needs gym, pybullet and numpy, and package code never imports or runs the clone. The package therefore serves only the pure Python fake (backends {'fake': '.fake:FakeCausalWorld'}); a sim backend would call gymnasium.make(None) and fail with MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY. The fake is a kinematic stand-in for the default reaching task: 9 normalized joint-position action values and a 37-element normalized structured observation, matching the upstream sizes (action.py:21-24, :61-64; reaching.py:47-51, :85-89), so no array is reduced. It uses Python's random.Random for the start joints (upstream seeds numpy) and models no PyBullet contacts, friction, PD controller, 4 ms physics substeps, pixel observations or interventions; it was never compared with the upstream simulator. NOT COVERED: the real TriFinger, the other task generators, pixel observations, interventions, rendering, and the upstream PyBullet model itself. Fidelity: analytic/F0, seeded (seed_control parameter), 40 ms control step (10 PyBullet substeps of 4 ms), realtime_factor 0, lockstep clock, full reset, snapshot_restore false; the upstream get_state/set_state (causalworld.py:492-521) is not implemented by the fake, so determinism is not claimed exact. Five warnings are expected of this Gymnasium family driver: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (it only stores the seed for the next reset and makes no native call) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived inputs (seed twice, ticks and action.values). G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. Only catalogue classes (cap.world.step.v1, cap.world.reset.v1, cap.world.seed.v1) are used, so there are no catalogue requests. A step with ticks 0 or 10001 is refused as MHS.CAPABILITY.INPUT_INVALID by the bridge schema, while action.values outside -1..1 is refused with MHS.SAFETY.ENVELOPE_VIOLATION; test_driver.py checks both. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the check printed.
